\textbf{Source.} Tadelis (2013), \emph{Game Theory: An Introduction}, Exercise 4.2 ``Weak Dominance'', p.~76 {[}PDF 95{]}. Reproduced verbatim. Answer in the source: none in the book (the preface, p.~xiii, says about half are solved on Princeton UP's website; not checked).

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Weak Dominance:} We call the strategy profile \(s^W \in S\) a \textbf{weakly dominant strategy equilibrium} if \(s_i^W \in S_i\) is a weakly dominant strategy for all \(i \in N\), that is, if \(v_i(s_i, s_{-i}) \ge v_i(s_i', s_{-i})\) for all \(s_i' \in S_i\) and for all \(s_{-i} \in S_{-i}\).

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\alph{enumi}.}
\item
  Provide an example of a game in which there is no weakly dominant strategy equilibrium.
\item
  Provide an example of a game in which there is more than one weakly dominant strategy equilibrium.
\end{enumerate}
\end{quote}
